presentation._comment_shadow_opacity: Stormwood's scene authors a 0.68 canopy-shadow floor for its permanent storm. WorldLook reapplies the global sun defaults after scene setup, so every phase must carry that realm-local value explicitly; Break alone returns to fully hard shadows, as the surge brief specifies.
presentation._comment_reapply: WorldLook re-merges its whole look per set_weather call, so the weather layer is re-applied every reapply_fading_seconds during a cross-fade and every reapply_steady_seconds otherwise (to follow the day clock). The ceiling updates every frame.
presentation._comment_floors: Review R2-2 / round-2 judge (a),(b): the storm horizon (and fog, which equals it) never falls below horizon_fraction of the native horizon luminance for the hour, and the ceiling never below ceiling_fraction of it, keeping each phase's authored hue. Round 3: horizon_fraction 0.55 (was 0.65; the pinned storm has no night) so Break's horizon can sit below Building's and Calm's in the monotonic ladder. Night Break stays violet-indigo instead of sinking to black; day Break's sky reads as a storm afternoon, not night. Ceilings are fully opaque (no sun/moon ghost through them); only Fading's breakup opens gaps, and only by day.
presentation._comment_rain: Stormwood's own rain emitter (world_weather.gd builds it hidden and Meadows-sized). The near layer is centred horizontally on the ACTIVE CAMERA and vertically on the ground: it spawns in spawn_band_above_ground_m over the higher of the terrain under the camera and the trainer, and lives lifetime_s, so drops fall through the foreground instead of the old camera-centred 14 m column where a measured 72-75% of drops were underground and ~2% reached the bottom 45% of the frame (WO-F10-07). max_drops is the Break (amount 1.0) count; each phase's rain_amount scales it. Streaks are thin tapered translucent spindles (streak_width_m is the base diameter) that fade in/out over life (fade_in/out_fraction); wind_slant tilts the fall (x, z per unit of fall) and streaks align to their velocity. The ring is shifted upwind by upwind_offset_fraction of the drift and its inner radius is derived as lens_clearance_m + the larger drift share + the 2-degree spread drift + the streak's sideways half-extent, ring_width_m wide; unit tests hold every drop >= 1.5 m from the lens, check rain reaches within 3 m of the trainer and that the foreground (bottom 45% of the view) gets rain. A physics roof over the camera's framed subject or the camera fades the near layer out over roof_fade_seconds (canopy and rod radius ignored). The emitter never sits more than max_height_above_ground_m above that floor; camera_height_offset_m is the fallback when the ground is unknown. far_layer (explicit radii, own lifetime/height, centre_offset_m above the near centre) is shorter and fainter. Round 3 (blind judge 8: Break's rain read as 'sparse thin streaks'): the near sheet is 1600 drops and the far layer 1700 at Break, and curtain_layer adds a distant curtain of 800 long faint streaks 32-62 m out; Break draws 4100 in all (was 2300), every phase scales them by rain_amount. At night each layer's tint follows the night factor down to its night_floor and alpha drops to its night_alpha_fraction; the near layer keeps a higher floor so night rain reads over the grass, the far layer a low one so the sky never looks like snow.

rain._comment_near_fade: WO-F09-05 round 2 (blind judge: a near streak rendered as a thick white pole): near_fade_m [gone, full] fades a streak by its view depth, so drops closer than the first value are invisible and fade in by the second.

presentation._comment_telegraph: Ground warning retains the combat hazard purple and exact strike.radius_m boundary as fine broken marks. Six jagged ground leaders converge on the contact point; bright tips move inward over strike.telegraph_seconds and the final quarter increases charge. No opaque zone disc. Reduced motion retains this continuous countdown without rim modulation. Terrain sampling and depth testing remain; no gameplay changes.

telegraph._why_fill: F10#3 round 2 (code-blind judge: an empty dashed outline read as a target selector and t080 looked like t110): a translucent fill from the first frame (fill_alpha), a stronger band the leader heads leave behind as they close on the contact point (charged_fill_alpha), and in the final ramp a solid rim over a brighter zone (final_fill_alpha).

presentation._comment_storm_base: OWNER DIRECTION (WO-F10-08): 'We should not have day and night in stormwood. It should just always be that kind of purple rainy sky regardless of time of day', including after the Long Storm is broken. stormwood_surge.gd hands this realm's WorldLook a config in which every time-of-day preset is reference_time plus overrides, so sky, clouds, fog, ambient, exposure and the key light's angle, energy and colour are the same at every hour; the world clock, is_dark(), night rest and encounter timing keep running. pin_time_of_day false restores the clock-blended look. The overrides keep the painted clouds and sun colour in the purple family.
presentation._why_f10_3_building_fading: F10#3 (coordinator/owner direction 2026-09-27 13:05, #356): Building and Fading carry distinct presentation, not only more or less of the same. Building's in-cloud sheet flicker rises 0.15 -> 0.22 (the storm gathering). Fading opens gaps where the cloud body is thin (ceiling_breakup 0.38, the shader's existing clearing parameter; the same at every hour), so the sky visibly clears; the ceiling stays opaque elsewhere, so no ghost sun disc shows. Existing shader parameters only.
presentation._comment_phases: OWNER DIRECTION (WO-F10-08, round 2): 'I like the building and break pictures. The other two aren't fantastic enough.' Every phase and the aftermath sit in the deep purple family (sky, ceiling, fog, key and ambient); nothing pale lavender or grey. Round 3 (blind judge 8 swapped Calm and Fading twice, so each phase gets a structural signature, not just more or less rain): the sky darkens and saturates monotonically Calm -> Building -> Break (ceiling luminance 0.43 / 0.40 / 0.37, saturation 0.29 / 0.35 / 0.42; Building is never brighter or greyer than Calm). Calm: straight-down light rain (wind 0, rain 0.3, half of Fading's opening rain), slow ceiling, no steam or lightning. Building: heavier slanted rain, fast ceiling, faint in-cloud flicker. Break: full rain with the distant curtain, fastest ceiling, strikes plus decorative sky lightning (sky_lightning) and in-cloud sheet glow. Fading carries Break over and lets it go: its `ramp` ({key: [start, end, power]} over the phase's progress) opens with Break's slant and 0.6 rain and straightens and thins them, while low ground steam (steam block) and a warm-violet afterglow low in the clouds decay to zero (ART_DIRECTION 3.3 'post-strike steam or afterglow'). The aftermath is the still deck: almost no motion but a defined, high-contrast cloud deck with lit rims and thin spots (ceiling_definition / ceiling_rim / ceiling_thin_glow). `intensity` (0..1) is a read-only hook (surge_intensity()). fog_colour follows sky_horizon (art.json's seam rule). No red: oxblood is Team Tether's.
presentation._why_f10_4_restored_sky: F10#4 (coordinator 13:20, #356; VIS F10#4 FAIL fix list), inside WO-F10-08's purple band: the aftermath lifts toward a restored sky without turning blue. Key light 0.45 -> 0.6 and ambient 0.62 -> 0.75; fog thins 0.0006 -> 0.0003; the deck softens (ceiling_contrast 0.6 -> 0.45, still above Calm's 0.3; definition 0.7 -> 0.5) while its lit rims and thin-spot glow rise (rim 0.3 -> 0.45, thin_glow 0.18 -> 0.3), so the clouds read as breaking light rather than a hard card. Sky colours, rain and stillness are unchanged.

aftermath_scar._why: F10#4 (coordinator 13:20, #356): after long_storm_ended the Struck Sentinel's live cyan strike scar cools to a dark violet seam in the purple band and its StrikeAfterglow light goes out; the spent strike reads as a scar, not a live bolt.

presentation._comment_aftermath: OWNER RULING (WO-F10-08): Stormwood stays purple after the Long Storm is broken; 'the aftermath shows only through lighter rain, no lightning and the scars'. Every aftermath phase (`all`) is the stillest version: the lightest drizzle (0.08), the gentlest wind (0.3), an almost still ceiling (speed 0.002), no flashes, sheet glow, steam or afterglow (and no ramp), the least fog and a steady key. Round 3 (blind judge 8: 'a flat, blank lavender card'): the still deck gets structure, a defined high-contrast cloud body (ceiling_definition, contrast 0.6) with lit rims and thin spots (ceiling_rim, ceiling_thin_glow), in the deep purple. The shorter aftermath Surge durations (aftermath_seconds) are unchanged gameplay; real strikes in an aftermath Break still telegraph and strike (rules), but no ambient flashes are added.
presentation._comment_steam: Round 3: Fading's ground steam (stormwood_surge.gd _build_steam): soft procedural billboards (generated radial-gradient texture, no texture art) rising slowly from a ring inner_radius_m..outer_radius_m around the framed subject. max_puffs is the count at steam 1.0; each row's `steam` (Fading's ramp eases it 1 -> 0) scales it. Unshaded, in the storm's purple-grey.
presentation._comment_sky_lightning: Round 3 (blind judge 8: Break had no lightning a still or strip could catch; its thin white horizon sliver read as a low sun): decorative Break-only sky lightning, no telegraph and no damage. Every interval_min..interval_max seconds an event: a distant cloud-to-ground bolt (bolt_chance; a jagged ribbon in the strike's white-violet bolt_distance_min_m..max_m away, top fading out of the cloud, lit cloud above it) or an in-cloud flash lighting the cloud body around one direction (cloud_flash_size is its cos-space radius), with flicker_chance of one weaker flicker. The existing whole-scene distant flash (flash block, 9-16 s, <= 0.35) is the occasional scene flash. UX 8 photosensitivity: every flash onset, including echoes and real strikes, counts; decorative onsets are refused while the last second holds max_flashes_per_second (code clamps to <= 3) less strike_reserve, so with a real strike no second ever holds more than 3. Nothing above the horizon band flashes whole-sky white. Reduced motion: cloud flashes are scaled by flash.reduced_motion_scale (0.15), flickers and restrikes are dropped, and bolts stay visible and are held reduced_motion_bolt_hold times longer instead of flickering.

sky_lightning._why_hold: F10#3 blind judge: a decorative bolt in view during a real ground warning read as already striking elsewhere; stormwood_lightning.gd holds decorative bolts for the telegraph plus 0.3 s and those events become in-cloud flashes.

presentation._comment_flash: Decorative sky flashes keep their established cadence and .2-.35 strengths. Ground impacts are identified by a local purple forked bolt with a pale core, converging ground leaders and local light instead of a full-frame white wash. strike_sky_strength caps their whole-scene request after the existing Break/distance gate; outside Break it still fades to zero at strike_sky_range_m. Thus their sky contribution can be weaker than decorative flashes. The existing linear decay also makes the capped flash shorter. Reduced motion applies reduced_motion_scale once to sky and local light, keeps the bolt and countdown, and disables warning rim modulation. strike_* configure the cached deterministic bolt and local light in stormwood_lightning.gd; no host scheduling RNG is consumed by visual geometry.

strike._why_spare_trainer_in_fight: Coordinator interim ruling 2026-09-25 (WO-F11-04, pending owner decision): while a trainer is committed to a creature fight, strikes do not target the trainer's position; they may still land as telegraphed hazards at the piloted creature, and strikes resume on the trainer when the fight ends. Host-authoritative and per peer. The earned witness measured 6 of 6 strikes on a trainer standing through one road fight (100 -> 0 health), because the stick drives the creature, not the trainer, during combat.
